in_latin.name: Siana
in_latin.long_meaning: Siana – derived from the Latin word gratia, meaning 'grace.' This name may also be derived from the Latin word sanus, meaning 'healthy' or 'whole,' as the name Siana was borne by a woman who was healed of leprosy in the New Testament (Luke 17:11).

biblical_reference.note: This is the name of a woman who was healed of leprosy by Jesus in the New Testament. She is often referred to as the 'Samaritan woman' or the 'Syro-Phoenician woman,' as she was likely from the region of Syria or Phoenicia.
